headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure between Dify and transformers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses tools wired into agent/workflow apps, while transformers can read/write files and process example scripts/model files. A shared workspace makes attacker-controlled content from one agent plausibly parsed by the other as instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or mounted volume
IF Dify ingests files produced by transformers as tool inputs
IF transformers processes Dify-generated text as executable instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories or containers
Disable automatic file ingestion between the agents
Require manual review before any file from the other agent is parsed
Add provenance labels to exchanged files
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, and has broad network egress; transformers touches multimodal data and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive content can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF the agents share files containing knowledge base content, logs, or multimodal data
IF either agent forwards loaded file contents to external APIs
IF shared credentials or tokens are present in the workspace
mitigations: Store each agent's data in separate workspaces
Remove secrets from shared folders before execution
Block outbound network access except to approved endpoints
Review logs for accidental content propagation
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. Dify also supports multiple instances via shared state in a Dify server datastore, while transformers supports multiple instances without coordination primitives. That creates a realistic write/write conflict on shared mutable resources, with possible corruption or overwrites.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF Dify instances share server datastore state with transformers outputs
IF no external locking or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Make one agent read-only for shared resources
Back up mutable state before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform with tools wired into agent/workflow apps, so its outputs can become downstream inputs. transformers is a document-processing framework that can consume files and example scripts. If Dify-generated text is treated as authoritative by transformers, errors can cascade into incorrect processing or actions, though the profiles do not show direct autonomous action-taking.
conditions: IF transformers consumes Dify output without verification
IF Dify-generated facts are used as source text for downstream processing
IF downstream workflows act on transformed outputs automatically
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require schema validation on Dify outputs
Compare outputs against source documents before use
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, while transformers touches multimodal data. If regulated or personal data is placed into Dify and then processed by transformers, retention and residency obligations can diverge because neither profile documents matching compliance controls. The other agent is cited because the risk is the handoff between them.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge bases
IF the same data is then processed by transformers
IF retention or residency requirements differ across the two systems
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Purge logs after each run
Use separate retention policies per agent
Confirm data residency before processing
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware routing and deletion
